data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Chlorine-releasing antiseptics (EUSOL = Edinburgh University Solution of Lime: chlorinated lime + boric acid; Dakin's = sodium hypochlorite 0.25–0.5%)

## Mechanism of action
- Release hypochlorous acid → oxidises proteins → kills bacteria, fungi, viruses; dissolves necrotic tissue (chemical debridement)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Sloughy, infected, malodorous ulcers and wounds (short courses)
- Dilute bleach baths (0.005%) for atopic dermatitis with recurrent staphylococcal infection

## Dose & formulations
- Soaked gauze changed once or twice daily for a few days; bleach bath: ½ cup 6% bleach in a full tub, 10 min, twice weekly

## Adverse effects
- Toxic to fibroblasts and granulation tissue — delays healing with prolonged use; irritation, pain

## Contraindications
- Clean granulating wounds

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Chemical debridement of sloughy ulcers; stop once clean
- Dilute bleach baths in atopic dermatitis

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (EUSOL, 1% sodium hypochlorite — Dakin's solution) and ch.32. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
